prompt: A model predicting hospital readmission uses a column that is filled in after the patient was readmitted.
tells: filled in after the patient was readmitted
why: That column is only filled in after readmission happens, so it gives away the answer. Using information from the future is data leakage.
trap: The data isn't unfair; it's from the future.

prompt: Test accuracy is suspiciously perfect because the test rows were copies of training rows.
why: Test rows copied from training rows let the model score by memory, not skill. Test data mixing into training is leakage.
trap: The model may be fine; the test isn't.

prompt: A model predicting which customers will leave uses 'account closed date' as an input.
why: An account closed date only exists for customers who already left. An input that reveals the answer is leakage.
trap: It isn't the label; it's a leak of it.

prompt: A fraud model includes the investigator's final verdict among its inputs.
why: The investigator's verdict comes after the fact and basically is the answer. Feeding it in as an input is leakage.
trap: Using it as an input, not a label, is the problem.

prompt: A stock model was trained with tomorrow's price accidentally included.
why: Tomorrow's price isn't known when the prediction is made, so including it lets the model cheat. That's leakage.

prompt: The data was scaled using statistics from all rows before splitting off the test set.
tells: before splitting off the test set
why: Scaling used averages that included the test rows, so a little test information reached training. Even subtle mixing like this is leakage.
trap: The split happened, just too late.
